text.arabic_uthmani: وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَآءُ ۚ نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَن نَّشَآءُ ۖ وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

baseline.text: Böylece Yusuf'u o ülkede yerleştirdik; orada dilediği yere yerleşiyordu. Merhametimizi dilediğimize eriştiririz ve iyilik yapanların ödülünü boşa çıkarmayız.

findings.text: Bir zamanlar tek hücreye bağlı olan Yusuf'un dilediği yerde yerleşebilmesi, kişisel rahatlıktan öte başkalarını barındırıp ülke çapında hizmet verebilen mekânsal yetkiye dönüşür.

activation_trace.role: Supplies effective capacity and serves as the enabling condition for later self-placement.
Supplies the act of taking a station and converts capacity into situated agency.
Leaves the destination spatially indeterminate, making range rather than one residence salient.
Joins both willing clauses to selected objects and supports the nesting of human choice within divine choice.

changed_reading.after: Yusuf receives a divinely enabled range in which his delegated choosing is genuine but remains nested inside God's wider choosing.
changed_reading.before: Yusuf is given territory and may reside wherever he wants.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The enabling verb at word 2, self-placement at word 6, the open locative at word 8, and the paired willing verbs at words 9 and 13.
baseline_models.mechanism: Divine enablement creates a field of viable stations; Yusuf exercises real local choice within that field, while the repeated willing construction places his choice inside the wider divine choice of mercy's recipients.

activation_trace.role: Gives mercy a directed arrival at its mark rather than the character of diffuse favor.
Supplies tender mercy as the substance being deliberately delivered.
Defines the negated failure mode as value passing away or becoming irrecoverable.
Identifies the conserved value as recompense answering to work.
Anchors recompense in enacted good rather than status alone.

changed_reading.after: The verse depicts a precise mercy-delivery system paired with a guarantee that enacted good cannot disappear from the economy of consequence.
changed_reading.before: God grants mercy and promises not to withhold the reward of good people.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The reaching verb at word 10, mercy at word 11, and the no-loss reward clause at words 15 through 17.
baseline_models.mechanism: Mercy is routed to a selected recipient with the precision of an impact, while the closing clause prevents the value generated by good action from leaking away. Delivery and conservation form one economy.

activation_trace.role: Introduces a return upon the actor and lets emplacement carry a consequence-returning resonance.
Adds correspondence between counterparts and supports a deed-to-outcome matching mechanism.
The negated disappearance keeps the returning consequence from being broken or lost.
Makes work and its answering recompense explicit.
Supplies the good action whose consequence returns in changed form.

changed_reading.after: His new station can also be carried as a recompensive return in which enacted good comes back as a fitting, preserved consequence.
changed_reading.before: Yusuf's settlement and the reward maxim are adjacent but separable claims.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The self-stationing root at word 6 is followed by the explicit no-loss recompense clause.
baseline_models.mechanism: Alongside ordinary settlement, the station can resonate as something returning upon its bearer and matching deed with consequence. The achieved place is then not merely a gift after goodness but a form of goodness coming back without being lost.

activation_trace.role: Supplies confinement in a bounded place as the initial spatial condition.
Adds prolonged remaining in place, intensifying the loss of spatial choice.
Provides the effective capacity that reverses prior spatial powerlessness.
Turns imposed placement into Yusuf's own act of taking a station.
Opens the formerly bounded spatial condition into an unspecified selectable range.

changed_reading.after: Enablement specifically reverses a history of coerced placement, converting a confined body into an agent who can distribute his presence across the land.
changed_reading.before: Enablement means that Yusuf gains high status and freedom of residence.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier space is coercive and prolonged; the focus verse reverses that spatial condition into empowered self-stationing across an open range. The change is not only elevation in rank but restoration of spatial agency.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies confinement, delay, enablement, and self-placement; I supply the reversal arrow from coerced location to restored spatial agency. A live alternative is simple promotion after release without making spatial reversal thematic.
structural_cues: A bounded prison is introduced at 12:36 and paired with prolonged staying at 12:42; 12:56 replaces imposed location with an open locative and self-placement.

activation_trace.role: Makes desire and willing explicit in the prior contest over Yusuf's agency.
Supplies active solicitation as pressure exerted on that desire.
Locates the pressure at the level of Yusuf's own self rather than only an external act.
Supplies confirmed stability and integrity as the condition under which agency is restored.
Reintroduces willing in a sanctioned, productive domain and contrasts it with coerced desire.
Gives the rehabilitated will an open spatial scope in which to operate.

changed_reading.after: Where he wills also marks the public rehabilitation of an agency that resisted manipulation and can now choose within a legitimate sphere.
changed_reading.before: Where he wills describes broad personal or administrative liberty.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context repeatedly stages another party trying to bend Yusuf's desire and self, then confirms his integrity. The focus verse's willing is therefore readable as rehabilitated agency: a will once pressured by solicitation is granted a legitimate field of action.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies pressured desire, the self under pressure, verified integrity, and later willing; I infer that the later spatial choice repairs the earlier assault on agency. The live alternative is that the willing clause denotes administrative latitude with no backward reference.
structural_cues: The confession at 12:51 repeats the solicitation and self constructions; vindication and appointment intervene before the focus verse grants a sphere for Yusuf's willing.

activation_trace.role: Supplies appointment by transforming a person into an office-bearing condition.
Defines the requested office as active custodianship rather than possession.
Makes watchful protection the function that spatial authority must perform.
Converts the requested custodial function into effective institutional capacity.
Provides the territorial field across which custodianship operates.
Makes station-taking a repeatable operational action within that field.
Allows deployment to remain responsive to need rather than tied to one fixed seat.

changed_reading.after: Yusuf can station himself wherever the custodial system requires, so freedom of place functions as infrastructure for public stewardship.
changed_reading.before: Yusuf may settle anywhere because he now possesses exceptional freedom and status.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding request and appointment concern guarded stores for the whole land. Against that frame, self-placement wherever needed becomes operational jurisdiction and mobile stewardship, not private residential privilege.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies appointment, stores, guarding, territorial enablement, and flexible stationing; I infer the arrow from flexible stationing to a distributed logistics role. A live alternative is that the language only denotes secure residence and broad political rank.
structural_cues: The focus verse directly follows Yusuf's request to be placed over the land's storehouses on the grounds of preservation and knowledge.

activation_trace.role: Supplies managed growth as the material base of the rescue mechanism.
Turns deliberate leaving-in-place into a preservation operation rather than abandonment.
Adds protective enclosure, explaining how value survives the consuming years.
Supplies descending rain as the ecological form in which relief reaches the people.
Preserves the split root's distress-relief image and makes the same event social rescue as well as rainfall.
Echoes rain descending and settling, giving mercy a material arrival pattern.
Names the compassionate force expressed through the ecological and administrative chain.
Defines what foresight blocks: the disappearance of stored value and enacted good.

changed_reading.after: Mercy reaches people through an ecological-administrative chain that preserves growth against future consumption, making non-loss both moral assurance and public method.
changed_reading.before: Mercy is a general divine favor illustrated by Yusuf's promotion.

context_deltas.mechanism: The agricultural plan grows, leaves, encloses, and preserves grain until rain and relief arrive. This sequence activates the focus verse's mercy as materially routed rescue and its no-loss clause as an anti-waste principle implemented through foresight.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies cultivation, deliberate retention, enclosure, rain-relief, mercy, and non-loss; I infer that Yusuf's administrative chain is one means by which mercy reaches its mark. The live alternative is to keep the agricultural plan and the theological maxim as parallel but unjoined layers.
structural_cues: The ordered movement from cultivation at 12:47, through protected reserves at 12:48, to rain and relief at 12:49 precedes the appointment and focus verse.

activation_trace.role: Supplies the emergence of previously obscured truth as the start of public repair.
Adds a fixed due or entitlement, allowing vindication to demand a consequential correction.
Confirms durable integrity as the basis for restoring Yusuf's standing.
Supplies purification after mixture, marking separation from the accusation that distorted his status.
Activates recompense as straightening and stabilizing what had been bent.
Locates the repair in Yusuf's changed public standing and condition.
Guarantees that neither prior integrity nor the correction answering it disappears.

changed_reading.after: The office also repairs a distorted public trajectory, straightening status around disclosed truth while preserving the ordinary recompense reading.
changed_reading.before: Yusuf's office is a reward paid after his innocence becomes known.

context_deltas.mechanism: Truth emerges, entitlement is fixed, integrity is confirmed, and Yusuf is extracted from prior contamination before he is established. The unusual repair branch of reward then reads the new station as a setting-right of a bent public history, not merely payment added afterward.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies disclosure, fixed right, integrity, purification, changed standing, and a repair branch under reward; I supply the arrow that establishment repairs the bent social record. The ordinary payment sense remains live and is cleaner morphologically.
structural_cues: Public confession and confirmation at 12:51 are followed by extraction for the king at 12:54 and establishment at 12:56.

activation_trace.role: Locates the earlier struggle in the inward faculty of judgment and impulse.
Gives the self's pressure an imperative force that requires restraint.
Supplies mercy as the stated interruption of inward moral pressure.
Carries that same compassionate force outward toward selected recipients.
Marks enacted good as the public fruit of inwardly governed agency.

changed_reading.after: Mercy first governs the agent from within and then, through the trustworthy agent, becomes public governance that reaches others.
changed_reading.before: Mercy in the focus verse is an external favor that grants Yusuf power.

context_deltas.mechanism: Mercy first appears as the exception that interrupts the self's commanding pressure toward wrong; it then appears in the focus verse as a force reaching chosen recipients. The same mercy can therefore underwrite both inward moral government and outward public government.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies inward command, mercy as exception, enacted good, and later public mercy; I infer that inward restraint enables trustworthy outward rule. A live alternative treats the two mercy statements as general formulas without a governance sequence.
structural_cues: Mercy interrupts the commanding self at 12:53, trust and office follow at 12:54 through 12:55, and mercy is redistributed socially at 12:56.

activation_trace.role: Places enacted good before release or office, separating moral identity from later status.
Recalls the earlier moral identity at the moment of worldly establishment.
Names the recompense whose preservation spans the change in status.
Repeats recompense beyond the focus verse and prevents office from closing the account.
Moves the reward horizon to a later and other register.
Ranks that later register as superior rather than merely additional.

changed_reading.after: His rise manifests preserved recompense without exhausting it; goodness precedes office, and the account remains open into a better later horizon.
changed_reading.before: The no-loss maxim explains Yusuf's worldly rise as the reward for his goodness.

context_deltas.mechanism: Yusuf is recognized as a doer of good while still confined, the focus verse connects establishment with preserved recompense, and the next verse names a better later recompense. Earthly office is therefore a real return but cannot exhaust the reward claim.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies pre-office goodness, worldly establishment, repeated recompense, and a better later register; I infer that the office is a partial manifestation rather than payment in full. A live alternative is that worldly mercy and later reward are categorically separate.
structural_cues: The same good-doer root frames Yusuf in prison at 12:36 and the maxim at 12:56; the next verse repeats reward and explicitly places a better form later.

remaining_uncertainties: The return-and-equivalence branches under self-placement may remain a secondary resonance rather than enter primary rendering.
The ecological and generative habitat reading is coherent but depends on cross-domain material analogy.
The split-root allotted-share reading is intentionally exploratory because the dominant mapped root gives the cleaner verbal mechanism.
The exact relation between worldly office and later reward remains open: partial manifestation and categorical separation are both live.
strongest_changes: The prison sequence turns enablement into a reversal from coerced location to restored spatial agency.
The storehouse appointment recasts flexible settlement as distributed public stewardship.
Cultivation, protected reserves, and rain-relief make mercy a materially routed rescue and non-loss an administrative method.
Vindication activates recompense as repair of a bent public status, while the next verse keeps reward from being exhausted by office.
summary.what_was_special: The focus sustained simultaneous readings of nested wills, precise mercy delivery, recompensive return, repaired status, and productive conservation. Split mappings and material branches preserved odd but traceable activations without displacing the ordinary senses.

activation_trace.role: Activates a specifically assigned share and recasts mercy's arrival as allotment.
Adds a fixed measure or basis, sharpening the idea that the share is proportioned.
Identifies mercy as what is experimentally heard as apportioned.
Adds the contextual image of a work-linked assigned return, connecting allotment to office and service.
Keeps the allotment resonance tied to recompense rather than arbitrary distribution.

changed_reading.after: At the exploratory split-root edge, mercy also resembles an assigned and measured share, with office and recompense appearing as apportioned responsibilities and returns.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant mapped root for the verb at word 10, while the ordinary directed-arrival reading is morphologically cleaner. It remains anchored to the supplied split inventory and the adjacent mercy-reward construction; downstream prose should present it only as an experimental allotment resonance, not as a replacement derivation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The reaching verb at word 10, mercy at word 11, and recompense at word 16.

activation_trace.role: Supplies protected internal incubation as the outlier's material starting point.
Turns the land into a receptive growing medium rather than only territory.
Provides the inhabitable station that contains and supports development.
Adds a generative enclosure and makes mercy habitat-forming.
Supplies descending moisture that completes the habitat's growth mechanism.
Shows growth emerging through rain and gives the material analogy contextual traction.

changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, mercy forms a protected, fertile habitat in which Yusuf's capacity matures into public provision.
changed_reading.before: God places Yusuf securely in a territory and favors him.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The egg, womb, fertile ground, rain, and abode branches create a deliberately cross-domain image and are too distant to control lexical translation. They remain valid as a focus-anchored material analogy reinforced by the agricultural sequence; downstream prose should label this an incubatory image, not an etymological claim.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Enablement at word 2, land at word 5, abode-taking at word 6, mercy at word 11, and the reaching verb at word 10.

activation_trace.role: Activates productive property as something protected from dissipation.
Adds vocation and earning, linking non-loss to sustained productive practice.
Supplies material safekeeping as the contextual means of preventing productive loss.
Adds active guarding and keeps the economic resonance tied to ethical custody.
Connects productive preservation back to work and its deserved return.
Prevents the economic echo from detaching from enacted good.

changed_reading.after: At a secondary economic resonance, ethical custody also keeps productive estates, vocations, and their returns from being dissipated.
changed_reading.before: God never lets the moral reward of good action vanish.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates noun branches for estate and vocation beneath a verbal no-loss construction. The roots remain exact and the storehouse context makes productive preservation visible; downstream prose should render it as an economic echo of the moral claim, never as its sole syntax.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The no-loss verb at word 15, recompense at word 16, and enacted good at word 17.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Former confinement reverses into mobile settlement.** م ك ن B005 (enablement), ب و ء B001 (settling/preparing an abode), ح ي ث B001 (indeterminate place), and ش ي ء B001 (willing) turn Yusuf from one held in a fixed cell into one who can establish himself across the land. The reading change is spatial agency.
2. **Mercy hits its recipient without losing recompense.** ص و ب B003 (aiming and hitting), ر ح م B001, ض ي ع B001 (causing loss), ء ج ر B001, and ح س ن B002 form a targeted-preservation mechanism. I infer that mercy reaches chosen persons while good work remains non-lost. Gift and recompense coexist rather than merge.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:58-100 filled the open geography with a specific restorative trajectory: brothers entered, family gathered, and the dream relation stood embodied.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Empowerment as the capacity to settle and prepare places.** The variants of `ب و ء:B001` jointly give “settling and preparing a place,” including being assigned an abode and enabling lodging. Joseph moves from summons and appointment (12:54-55) to choosing where to settle; 12:58-60 then shows brothers entering his provisioning domain. The packet supplies territorial freedom and later distribution; I infer that spatial emplacement becomes administrative reach. *Yatabawwaʾu minhā* reads not merely as personal comfort but as the ability to position himself where mercy-bearing work can operate.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:99 settles the reunited family safely in Egypt, extending Joseph's administrative emplacement from personal reach across the land to a secure place made available for others.

words.gloss_range: resumptive and connective opening particle that links the prior scene to a divine summary
words.prose: The opening word keeps the appointment scene connected while shifting the register into divine narration. It makes the establishment that follows feel like the narrated outcome of the previous sequence, not an isolated new report.

topics.headline: resumptive opening into divine summary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins by carrying the previous scene forward into a divine narrator summary.
topics.reason: The rows converge on continuity plus register shift at the ayah boundary.

words.gloss_range: comparison particle in the opening formula, marking the empowerment as happening in that recognized manner
words.prose: The word supplies the likeness relation in the opening frame. Before the main action is named, the reader is told to hear Joseph’s empowerment as an instance of a recognizable divine pattern, with the earlier Joseph establishment (12:21) and other elevation formulas (6:83; 28:14) in view.

topics.headline: comparison frame for empowerment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the event is framed as patterned divine action before the verb of establishment arrives.
topics.reason: The comparison particle governs the demonstrative and frames the following divine act.

words.gloss_range: distal demonstrative in the comparison frame, pointing back to a marked prior pattern or sequence
words.prose: The demonstrative completes the opening frame by pointing away from the immediate clause. Its distance lets the reader retrieve the earlier Joseph establishment (12:21), the prison-to-appointment sequence, and the larger divine pattern before the sentence names the act.

topics.headline: distal pointer to prior pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the main action is interpreted through a backward-looking pointer rather than introduced cold.
topics.reason: The demonstrative has discourse-supplied reference and stands before the main verb as the frame for it.

words.gloss_range: completed divine establishment that grants Joseph firm authority within a defined land-domain
words.prose: This verb makes the first major beat a completed divine act: Joseph does not seize status, he receives firm establishment. The construction gives both beneficiary and domain, so the authority is personal to Joseph and grounded in a land-field. Its recurrence with the earlier establishment scene (12:21) makes this moment feel like the authority-stage fulfillment of an earlier narrative hint, while broader tamkīn scenes can also carry responsibility and test pressure (6:6; 46:26).
words.root_gloss_range: firmness, place, station, and caused establishment; locally selected as divinely caused territorial empowerment

topics.headline: beneficiary and domain built into establishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grant has a named beneficiary and a governed field, not a flat claim that Joseph became powerful.
topics.reason: The verb is completed by the beneficiary phrase and the locative domain phrase.

topics.headline: Form II firm establishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the force of caused, firm installation rather than mere placement.
topics.reason: The Form II perfect and root field support caused establishment and firm station.

topics.headline: marked empowerment formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the local establishment as part of a marked Quranic and same-surah empowerment pattern, especially with 12:21.
topics.reason: The rows identify repeated local and cross-surah tamkīn patterns without requiring them to override the local parse.

topics.headline: human appointment reframed as divine act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prior royal appointment is re-read as completed divine agency.
topics.reason: The boundary rows show the subject shift from human scene to divine first-person action.

words.gloss_range: benefactive recipient marker attaching the establishment specifically to Joseph
words.prose: The particle marks Joseph as the recipient and beneficiary of the establishment. Its position before the land-domain keeps the grant directed to him before the sentence expands to where that grant operates.

topics.headline: benefactive recipient marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that empowerment is grammatically directed for Joseph before its territory is described.
topics.reason: The lām governs the proper name as the recipient complement of the establishment verb.

words.gloss_range: named foreign proper noun, grammatically governed as the beneficiary and kept explicit at the empowerment apex
words.prose: The name keeps the empowerment personal even though the ayah is moving toward universal maxims. Its diptote case-shape also lets the reader see a foreign proper name fitted into Arabic governance.

topics.headline: explicit named beneficiary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the formula remains anchored in Joseph as a named person before it opens into general principles.
topics.reason: The proper noun is explicitly governed by the recipient particle and closes the beneficiary unit.

topics.headline: foreign diptote case marking
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammatical precision of the name under genitive governance despite its fatḥa case-shape.
topics.reason: The foreign proper noun is governed by the preposition while retaining diptote behavior.

words.gloss_range: locative containment particle that makes authority operate inside the land-domain and bridges establishment to settling
words.prose: The preposition frames the domain as a sphere Joseph is established within, not simply an object placed under him or a detached rule-over claim. It also stands at the joint between the divine establishment and the later settling clause, so the land becomes both setting and arena; broad jurisdictional pressure remains local to Joseph’s narrative domain.

topics.headline: inside-domain rather than detached rule-over
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the authority is portrayed as embedded within the land-domain, while totalizing claims must stay limited to the local narrative scope.
topics.reason: The local preposition licenses containment and scope; it does not by itself prove unlimited world-wide jurisdiction.

words.gloss_range: definite land-domain, locally the known territory of Joseph’s empowerment while retaining concrete terrain and broader jurisdictional pressure
words.prose: The land is not a passive object of the verb but the governed sphere in which establishment and movement happen. The following clause keeps the noun alive as terrain from which Joseph can take up places, while same-surah echoes turn the brothers’ casting-place vocabulary (12:9) and the earlier establishment formula (12:21) into authority within land.
words.root_gloss_range: earth, land, ground, territory, and jurisdiction; locally a definite empowered domain made traversable by the following clause

topics.headline: governed definite land-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the land is the sphere of empowerment and movement, not the direct object acted upon.
topics.reason: The genitive locative phrase makes the land a governed domain.

topics.headline: definite territory with broad pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a definite, unified domain, while claims of total-earth jurisdiction are kept to rhetorical or formulaic pressure rather than made a local administrative fact.
topics.reason: The definite noun supports an identifiable broad domain, but local context keeps the sense anchored in Joseph’s known land setting.

topics.headline: land as narrative reversal and formula field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same land vocabulary turns from threatened displacement into empowered habitation, with the 12:21 formula returning at a higher stage.
topics.reason: The echo rows give concrete same-surah and formulaic links that enrich the local land-domain.

words.gloss_range: ongoing self-directed taking up of places from the land under the prior divine establishment
words.prose: The imperfect turns completed establishment into an ongoing condition: Joseph is now able to take up places from the land. Form V makes that settlement self-directed within the divine grant, and the following scope phrase turns territory into lived mobility rather than static office. The dwelling field can resonate with granted-settlement formulas such as paradise settlement wherever the saved will (39:74), while habitation remains the local sense.
words.root_gloss_range: settling, lodging, taking an abode, and in some contexts incurring or deserving; locally spatial self-placement is selected with moral reward resonance only as secondary pressure

topics.headline: ongoing circumstantial settling
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine establishment is immediately unpacked as Joseph’s continuing condition of free settlement.
topics.reason: The imperfect functions as a circumstantial explanation after the completed establishment.

topics.headline: Form V self-placement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices Joseph’s delegated agency: he takes up places for himself rather than merely being stationed.
topics.reason: The Form V shape and min-phrase support active self-placement from within the domain.

topics.headline: settlement and reward echoes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices dwelling and reward resonances, including the granted-dwelling pattern in 39:74, while habitation remains the selected local sense.
topics.reason: The broader b-w-ʾ field and echoes add resonance but do not replace local spatial settlement.

words.gloss_range: source and partitive particle in the suffixal phrase, making settlement drawn from portions of the land
words.prose: The particle keeps Joseph’s settling dynamic. He is not merely present in a fixed place; the phrase makes residence drawn from the land’s available portions before the next word opens that access to wherever.

topics.headline: source and partitive access
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Joseph’s movement draws from the land’s parts rather than resting in an undifferentiated location.
topics.reason: The source particle with the feminine suffix refers back to the land and stages the movement toward open scope.

words.gloss_range: locative wherever-adverb opening the settlement clause to an unbounded place-scope within the land
words.prose: This adverb turns the partitive source into open place-scope. It does not name a station; it lets Joseph’s settlement range wherever the will-clause selects, joining granted-liberty formulas such as garden or settlement freedom (7:19; 7:161; 39:74). Variant ending evidence changes grammatical coloring rather than the basic scope.

topics.headline: open locative scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the freedom is spatially open within the land rather than tied to a named station.
topics.reason: The indeclinable locative adverb is completed by the will-clause and opens the scope of settling.

topics.headline: qiraat ending as grammatical pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accepted ending variation marks the adverb as a case-sensitive pressure point without changing the wherever function.
topics.reason: The standard and variant endings preserve adverbial function while differing in final-vowel analysis.

topics.headline: wherever-will freedom formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase belongs to a recognizable granted-liberty pattern, including the granted dwelling formula in 39:74.
topics.reason: The echo rows give concrete formulaic parallels for wherever-plus-will wording.

words.gloss_range: effective will selecting the places of settlement; canonically Joseph’s delegated will, with a variant that shifts the slot to divine will
words.prose: In the standard reading, the word closes Joseph’s mobility clause with real delegated choice: he settles where he wills. The accepted variant can shift the willing subject to God, so the same slot becomes a theological pressure point, but the local function remains selection of where settlement occurs. The repeated will-root also fits Joseph’s larger story of divine exception and subtle arrangement (12:76; 12:100).
words.root_gloss_range: will, intending, and effective volition; locally place-selection in the settlement clause, then echoed by divine will in the mercy clause

topics.headline: Joseph’s delegated will
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Joseph’s authority includes operational choice, not only title or appointment.
topics.reason: The standard 3ms imperfect recovers Joseph as subject and governs the place-scope.

topics.headline: variant shifts willing subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reading tradition can make the same place-selection slot express direct divine will, while the canonical local parse still licenses Joseph’s delegated agency.
topics.reason: The variant is valid evidence for agency contrast but should not erase the standard surface reading.

topics.headline: paired will verbs in one ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah moving from Joseph’s will over place to God’s will over mercy.
topics.reason: The same root recurs at the close of the mobility clause and mercy clause.

words.gloss_range: divine causing mercy to reach selected recipients; corrected away from the input n-ṣ-b tag toward the hit/reach/bestow field
words.prose: This verb pivots from Joseph’s story to an ongoing divine principle. Its surface form is best read through the reach-or-hit field, not the input hardship root, so mercy becomes a directed arrival aimed at whomever God wills; the fall-or-rain image makes that arrival feel like beneficial mercy reaching its mark, not diffuse atmosphere.
words.root_gloss_range: reaching, hitting the mark, befalling, and beneficial arrival; locally causative delivery of mercy to a chosen recipient, with the alternate ṣ-y-b analysis in the same hit/reach field

topics.headline: surface form corrects the input root tag
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the mercy mechanism depends on directed reaching, not on importing the unrelated hardship or erecting field.
topics.reason: The surface form fits the reach/befall/bestow field and blocks the MASAQ n-ṣ-b assignment as a local root guide.

topics.blocking_evidence: The n-ṣ-b hardship or portion comparisons rely on the rejected upstream root tag rather than the local surface form.
topics.headline: wrong-root distribution imported from tag
topics.reason: The row’s useful warning is the mismatch; the n-ṣ-b distribution itself cannot govern this word.

topics.headline: directed mercy delivery
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices mercy as targeted arrival, not a static attribute or vague kindness.
topics.reason: The verb governs a mercy bāʾ phrase and an open recipient object.

topics.headline: story pivots to universal mercy principle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the tense and voice shift from Joseph’s completed establishment to God’s continuing rule of mercy allocation.
topics.reason: The 1cp imperfect opens the universal divine declaration after the narrative half.

words.gloss_range: bāʾ particle marking mercy as means, content, and manner of the reaching act
words.prose: The particle makes mercy inseparable from the delivery verb. It can be heard as the means, the content, and the manner of the act, so the recipient is reached in and by divine mercy before the recipient is even named.

topics.headline: mercy as means, content, and manner
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that mercy is foregrounded as the mode and substance of divine reaching before the recipient slot appears.
topics.reason: The bāʾ-governed phrase stands between the verb and recipient and licenses instrument/content/manner readings.

words.gloss_range: divine-owned mercy as the beneficial resource or medium delivered to selected recipients
words.prose: The suffix makes the mercy explicitly divine-owned, not an impersonal force. As a singular noun governed by the bāʾ phrase, mercy becomes the beneficial resource delivered to recipients; the womb-linked root image gives it nurturing and protective force rather than explicit forgiveness. Its pairing with reward later lets the ayah hold bestowed care and preserved recompense together, and the mercy-near-the-muḥsinīn pattern has a concrete counterpart at 7:56.
words.root_gloss_range: mercy, compassion, tender care, and womb-linked nurturing; locally possessed divine mercy delivered as positive bestowal rather than explicit forgiveness

topics.headline: possessed divine mercy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that mercy is attached to the same divine speaker who establishes, reaches, and refuses to waste reward.
topics.reason: The first-person suffix binds the mercy noun to the divine subject chain.

topics.headline: mercy as delivered beneficial care
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices mercy as an active beneficial resource, not merely an abstract attribute or explicit pardon formula.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the delivery construction and is not paired locally with forgiveness language.

topics.headline: mercy paired with will, excellence, and reward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah balancing bestowed mercy with protected reward and linking mercy to the muḥsinīn field, including 7:56.
topics.reason: The echo and structural rows connect mercy with will, excellence, and the later reward clause.

words.gloss_range: open relative recipient pronoun, selected by the following divine will verb
words.prose: The pronoun opens the recipient slot without naming a fixed class. The following will-verb then supplies the criterion, so mercy is available to an open whomever but actualized by divine selection.

topics.headline: open recipient slot selected by will
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the mercy recipient is not named by office or entitlement but left open for divine selection.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is object of the reaching verb and object within the will clause.

words.gloss_range: divine first-person will that selects who receives mercy
words.prose: The word closes the mercy maxim by making divine will the active criterion. It answers the open recipient pronoun and also echoes the earlier will verb, so Joseph’s spatial freedom and mercy’s distribution are heard in the same volitional field without becoming the same thing. The same root also belongs to Joseph-story turnpoints where divine will frames what can happen (12:76; 12:100).
words.root_gloss_range: will, intending, and effective volition; locally God’s operative selection of mercy recipients

topics.headline: divine will selects mercy recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the mercy clause gives no visible human criterion; the recipient is selected by God’s will.
topics.reason: The 1cp imperfect governs the relative object and closes the mercy clause.

topics.headline: will-based mercy beside excellence-based reward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah holding discretionary mercy and protected earned reward side by side.
topics.reason: The rows explicitly contrast the mercy recipient formula with the muḥsinīn reward clause.

topics.headline: will-root echoes across the ayah and story
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices repeated will vocabulary connecting this maxim with Joseph’s earlier mobility and wider narrative turnpoints.
topics.reason: The same root appears in the mobility clause and in broader Joseph-story will contexts.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector joining the positive mercy statement to the negative reward-preservation statement
words.prose: The connector makes the final guarantee an added partner to the mercy maxim. The ayah does not simply move to another topic; it coordinates active bestowal with refused loss.

topics.headline: coordination of mercy and reward principles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negative reward guarantee is joined to the mercy maxim as its counterpart.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the final negated clause with the preceding mercy declaration.

words.gloss_range: negative particle denying an ongoing divine disposition to waste the reward of excellent doers
words.prose: The negator turns the final clause into a standing guarantee. With the imperfect that follows, it denies not just one possible loss but a divine practice of letting earned reward disappear.

topics.headline: standing negation of reward-loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that reward-loss is categorically denied as a divine disposition, not merely absent in one case.
topics.reason: The negative particle scopes over the imperfect verb and its reward object.

words.gloss_range: negated divine causation of loss, specifically refusing to let or make earned reward disappear
words.prose: The verb makes the final guarantee sharper than saying reward remains. Form IV would make God the cause of loss, and the negation rules that out; the reward of excellent doers is protected from disappearance, neglect, and nullification. The same reward-preservation formula recurs across righteous-action contexts (9:120; 11:115; 18:30) and returns in Joseph’s own story at 12:90.
words.root_gloss_range: loss, wasting, disappearance, neglect, and causing something to be lost; locally negated Form IV as a reward-preservation guarantee

topics.headline: negated causative loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause denies God as cause of any loss or wasting of earned reward.
topics.reason: The Form IV imperfect is negated and takes reward as its object.

topics.headline: not-wasting-reward formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final verb as part of a recognized reward-preservation formula, including the return at 12:90.
topics.reason: The rows show strong co-occurrence with reward and exact or near-exact formulae.

topics.headline: closing counterpart to mercy delivery
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah pairing active mercy-delivery with refused reward-loss.
topics.reason: The final verb governs the closing beat and balances the positive causative verb earlier.

words.gloss_range: earned recompense or wage made the protected object of the non-waste guarantee
words.prose: The noun gives the guarantee a concrete object: the protected thing is recompense, not vague approval. Its construct relation binds that reward to the excellent doers, while the next ayah and 12:90 keep the reward theme moving beyond this clause.
words.root_gloss_range: hire, wage, recompense, reward, and due return; locally singular protected recompense belonging to excellent doers

topics.headline: reward as protected direct object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final guarantee protects a concrete recompense object belonging to excellent doers.
topics.reason: The noun is accusative as object of the negated loss verb and opens the construct phrase.

topics.headline: wage and recompense force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices reward as earned value due to action, not generic praise.
topics.reason: The semantics and local muḥsinīn complement activate recompense and earned-value force.

topics.headline: reward formula and forward bridge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reward noun starts a thematic chain through 12:57 and 12:90 rather than ending the discussion.
topics.reason: The echo rows connect the noun to immediate and later same-surah reward statements plus formulaic parallels.

words.gloss_range: definite active-participle class of excellent beneficent doers whose reward is protected
words.prose: The last word lands the ayah on a moral class rather than on Joseph’s office. Its active-participle form names people who do or produce excellence, and the definite plural lets Joseph’s case become an instance of a wider rule: the reward of such doers is not wasted. The same category is recognized within Joseph’s story (12:78; 12:90) and joins the mercy-nearness formula at 7:56.
words.root_gloss_range: goodness, beauty, excellence, beneficence, and doing good; locally Form IV active agents who produce iḥsān

topics.headline: definite class of excellent doers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the guarantee applies to a recognized category of active excellence, not to status, lineage, or appointment.
topics.reason: The definite plural active participle completes the reward construct and names the moral category.

topics.headline: Joseph included in universal category
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah moving from Joseph’s specific story into a class that includes him and others like him.
topics.reason: The final position and referent evidence support a tadhyīl-like universalizing move.

topics.headline: muḥsinīn echoes across reward and mercy formulas
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the closing word as an echo-node for same-surah recognition points and wider mercy-reward formulas, including 7:56 and 12:90.
topics.reason: The echo rows connect the class to reward, mercy, and Joseph-story recognition points.
